messages:
alex: Heads-up — we9re seeing steady KV cache memory growth on private onprem A100 nodes when serving very long contexts (>16k tokens). Hosted traces don't show it. Looks like fragmentation + repeated page allocations.

nina: Logs? any perf counters? :thinking_face:

alex: Quick summary:
- Repro with loadgen using 1x long prompt (20k tokens) + streaming.
- Memory graph shows GPU reserved rises over time, CPU rss slowly increases too.
- pmap shows many small anonymous mappings on the worker process.
- nvprof/nvtx shows frequent small cudaMemcpyHostToDevice spikes.

sam: That pattern smells like repeated host<->device copying of spilled KV pages. Could be our fallback kernel doing per-chunk memcpy instead of GPU-direct compact ops.

lee: Are kernels different between environments? Hosted uses precompiled kernel bundle A, Dedicated has B, Private (onprem) falls back to legacy kernels when driver < 525.

alex: Exactly. We ran kernel selector on onprem and it chose the generic "matmul_fallback" path for sparse attention + fp16 qkv. That path keeps KV in many small pinned host buffers and copies them each step.

anika: Oof. That would explain fragmentation — jemalloc gets a lot of mid-size frees/allocs and we end up with slab churn.

nina: Do we have a quick repro script? I can run perf on Dedicated tonight.

alex: Repro steps we used (short):
```
# on a dedicated/private node
git checkout perf/kvcache-debug
RUNTIME_KV_DEBUG=1 RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=auto ./bin/serve --model /models/llama-70b --max-tokens 20000 &
# run loadgen
./loadgen --seq-len 20000 --rate 1 --concurrency 2 --streaming
```
Then tail logs for `kv:alloc` / `kv:evict` lines. Also capture `pmap -x PID` and `perf record -g -p PID -- sleep 30`.

infra-bot: deploy-status: background job created to collect `pmap` and `nvprof` output from the failing host cluster (job id 8241).

sam: Early profiling notes:
- perf shows high time in `memcpy@plt` on CPU threads pinned to NVMe interrupts.
- GPU traces show many small host pinned buffer transfers (~64KB) instead of single larger batched xfer.
- jemalloc stats show high active / allocated ratio with many arenas.

lee: Interesting — Hosted likely benefits from our custom kernel pack which supports batched KV page uploads (coalesced copies). Dedicated got the pack but with a kernel selector config that prefers throughput kernels; Private onprem misses it entirely.

anika: Two possible mitigations:
1) Force kernel override on private to the coalescing path (env RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=coalesce) and re-run.
2) Increase `kv.compact_threshold_ms` from 5m -> 20m on Dedicated to avoid aggressive compaction that triggers churn.
3) Enable process-level hugepages / MADV_DONTNEED tuning and set MALLOC_CONF to reduce fragmentation.

alex: I pushed a quick patch to runtime that adds a heuristic: if avg KV memcpy size < 256KB and seq_len_peak > 8k, prefer coalescing kernel. Patch: https://git.redwood/perf/merge_requests/72

nina: Can we run experiment matrix: (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) x (kernel=auto,coalesce,legacy) x (kv.compact=5m,20m) and measure peak GPU reserved + cpu memcpy rate? I'll script it.

sam: Also add a test for batching heuristics — when batch size > 4 and seq_len > 8k we should ensure KV allocations are pre-sized to avoid mid-run growth.

lee: For onprem ops: need a note for infra about driver upgrade path. If driver < 525 we won't get the new kernels. Ops: schedule rolling node image that includes kernel bundle v2026-03.

anika: Small quick fix we can ship to reduce customer impact: set `RUNTIME_KV_MAX_FRAGMENT_BYTES=1048576` on Private clusters to force coalescing into 1MB chunks. Low risk.

alex: Agreed. I'll open a config rollout PR and add the experiment docs. Nina, assign me for data collection rows in your matrix.

nina: Assigned. I'll post results in this thread tomorrow.

sam: Thanks — if we confirm kernel selector bug we should backport the heuristic to patch branch for Dedicated.

infra-bot: job 8241 completed — artifact: s3://redwood-perf/8241/{pmap.txt,nvprof.nvvp,jemalloc.txt}

alex: Downloaded artifacts, initial glance matches the small-copy hypothesis. Will attach annotated screenshots to the MR.

anika: If anyone hits this on customer clusters, run `env RUNTIME_KV_DEBUG=1 RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=coalesce` and collect `pmap` + `jemalloc.stats`.

lee: Adding a checklist for ops: driver check, kernel bundle version, set fragment env, monitor kv.alloc/evict counters in console.

nina: Cool. Will close loop once matrix runs finish. :v:
